name: clinical_v0_bounded_negative_tail
rationale: Composed final-layer weights identify units 198 and 38 as positive readout paths that activate for high normalized values. In 128 calibration patients, their active cases remain underestimated after the original affine correction; almost all are measured variables rather than static/administrative channels. Increase only these two effective output coefficients by 1%, a fixed conservative expansion of the existing learned paths. Negative GELU-tail contributions change in the opposite direction, also consistent with the common positive offset in the low/middle range. No fitting, gradients, optimizer or test data. A second, bounded path partly reverses the affine edit's extra expansion of negative unit 20 only above preactivation 2, capped beyond 4. Calibration residuals remain positive at activations 0-2 but turn negative above 2, so a global gain reversal would be inappropriate. Units 246 and 226 have negligible original effective coefficients and are repurposed to implement c*(GELU(16*(z20-2))-GELU(16*(z20-4)))/16, c=-0.005*original_coefficient20. The coefficient follows algebraically from the earlier fixed 0.5% gain change; no coefficient is fitted to targets. This is one specified hypothesis, not a parameter sweep.
